info.description:
MESL Finance: the money, members, fees and assets of the lab.
PostgreSQL owns every rule (db/schema.sql); these endpoints call them in one
transaction each and translate what they refuse — nothing here invents a rule.

The money in one breath:
- Every income lands first in the envelope named "Unallocated General" (the pool):
  `POST /envelopes` never creates it (the bootstrap does) and `POST /deposits`
  without `envelope_id` is where it goes.
- The committee then splits the pool with `POST /allocation-suggestion` (dry run)
  and `POST /allocations` (the real split).
- Members owe weekly fees (B-05): `POST /deposits` with `source="weekly_fee"`
  and the member id; refunds go back out through `POST /refunds` — both move
  only the pool.
- An event or project tracks its own money through a cost center:
  in via deposits/expenses with `cost_center_id`, watched at
  `GET /cost-centers/{id}/summary`, leftovers swept back with `POST /sweeps`
  (B-16).
- Month end: `GET /dues` is who owes what; `POST /reconciliations` records the
  pocket-notes count, `GET /reconciliation-status` / `/unverified-entries` /
  `/difference-suspects` say what still needs a look (B-20). `GET /health`
  runs the database's own integrity checks.
- When a committee hands over, `POST /tenures/close` locks the closed tenure,
  writes the snapshots and opens the next one (B-18/B-25).

Rules you would otherwise think are bugs:
- **Money amounts are immutable** — no entry is ever updated or deleted
  (db/schema.sql: append-only + checksums). A wrong amount is CORRECTED, not
  edited: the fix/`fix-amount` endpoints write a reversal plus a replacement in
  one transaction; labels (note, tag, source, date...) stay editable through
  the `edit-labels` action, and every old value is kept in the history tables.
- Every error everywhere is RFC 9457 problem+json: `{code, detail, status,
  title, type}` — the `code` is machine-readable ("rule_violation" means
  PostgreSQL refused; "unknown_reference" names a dead pointer).
- Envelope/cost-center/member lists are id-ordered and never carry computed
  balances; balances are ledger reads.

Read `/redoc` for the per-feature walkthroughs summarized under each tag.

(inactive envelope, pre-tenure date, no open tenure) 409.

EVERY member's standing as of today (B-09): what they owe, their credits,
where unpaid weeks started.

with the numbers (B-09). Payments: ledger deposit `source="weekly_fee"`;
refunds, waivers, donations and corrections go to their own tags.

post.description:
Committee handover in one action (B-25): three things happen in one transaction.

1. the OPEN tenure locks forever on `close_on` (a date older than the last
recorded entry is refused, 409 `rule_violation`);
2. member / asset / holding snapshots are written — the reads below;
3. the NEXT tenure named `next_name` opens on close_on + 1 and, when the
closed one had ledger lines, a carry-over `opening` entry lands in it
(db/schema.sql:925-936). Closed tenures never change again (B-18).

tags.description: Log in. The treasurer's username/password come from server settings (D-006); the bearer JWT they return is accepted by every other route
tags.name: auth

tags.description: The money ledger: deposits in, expenses out, transfers between envelopes, and the corrections (fix-amount, edit-labels). MONEY IS IMMUTABLE (D-080/B-18): fix-amount writes a reversal + a replacement in ONE transaction — there is no edit or delete endpoint, by design. `GET /entries` lists the current truth (fixed entries collapse into one line); it carries NO amounts on purpose (db/schema.sql:426-430)
tags.name: ledger

tags.description: Where money may sit. The pool is named "Unallocated General" and is created by the first-start bootstrap, never here (D-041); every other envelope maps a purpose: member projects, lab projects, events, competitions, research, admin (B-15). Cap + priority are allocation inputs (D-021): the suggestion and `POST /allocations` fill capped envelopes first by priority, the rest by the previous session's shares. `deactivate` only works at zero balance
tags.name: envelopes

tags.description: One cost center per event, member project, lab project or competition; tag money with it as it moves (ledger's `cost_center_id`). The summary shows in/out/swept/leftover; at an event's end the leftover is swept back to the pool (B-16/B-17) — no overspend warnings exist on purpose. Kind is fixed at create
tags.name: cost-centers

tags.description: Who belongs to the lab, membership periods (start once, end once), and the ledger-side adjustments: waivers (owed week excused), credit donations, opening balances, corrections. Periods overlap nothing: two open periods are refused (db/schema.sql:101-102). No auto-expulsion exists (B-09) — dues show raw numbers
tags.name: members

tags.description: The weekly rate (per member, whole BDT; a rate change only affects future weeks, B-05), shutdown weeks (a national-vacation range that forgives whole weeks, B-08 — undo a mistake by re-entering the same range with `is_shutdown=false`, newest row wins), and `GET /dues`: every member, what they owe, credits, and when arrears started. A member's fee payment is a deposit with source `weekly_fee` (ledger tag)
tags.name: fees

tags.description: What the lab owns and holds. Choose: mode `individual` = one unit per row (a device, a multimeter serial by tag), mode `counted` = a quantity per row (kits, components); `ownership` admin = came from the college admin (their damaged items queue for replacement, `/replacement-queue`), lab = lab money bought it (db/schema.sql:639-640). Consumables are never tracked (B-21). RECORDING A PURCHASE: record the expense first (`POST /expenses`), then the acquisition (kind `acquired`, source `purchase`) must name that payment in `ledger_transaction_id` — that link is the item's only cost record (D-163, db/schema.sql 0002). A lent/lost/damaged event names who had it (member_id), damage needs a note (db/schema.sql rules), lend-to-nothing is refused. Fix an event via `/events/{event_id}/fix` (reversal + replacement), never an edit
tags.name: assets

tags.description: The database's self-check (`verify_all`): an empty `[]` means healthy, problem strings otherwise. Bearer token required: it exposes money detail
tags.name: health

tags.description: Month-end check that pocket notes and the machine agree (B-20). Count what you hold per envelope, `POST /reconciliations` — matched/answer says pass or difference. After a match, `/unverified-entries` shrinks to what came since; `/difference-suspects` guesses which entry explains a difference (the basics: an extra zero, swapped digits, a same-amount transfer). Entries before the last match never need review, and nothing to reconcile yet is refused (B-20)
tags.name: reconciliation

tags.description: Committee handover (B-25): `POST /tenures/close` closes the open tenure on close_on (never before the last entry), writes member/asset/holding snapshots, opens the NEXT tenure named `next_name` on close_on+1, and carries balances over as an `opening` entry. The closed tenure is locked forever (B-18); the snapshots are the handover register
tags.name: tenures
